pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks every seeded item has done=0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test checks / and /?view=open list only open items in id order.
'AC-3' test checks done view lists ✓-marked done items in id order (ids 3,1 marked → First, Third).
'AC-4' test checks all view lists everything in order with ✓ only on done.
'AC-5' asserts exact nav HTML for each view and the default; current is <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty, __proto__; code uses Object.hasOwn.
'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views.
traffic/routes.json contains both routes; 'AC-8' test asserts them.

findings.what: The test 'on a due minute hits /healthz and every listed route' was loosened from toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES]) to expect(app.seen.map(...)).toBeDefined(), which can never fail. It no longer proves the Worker requests healthz and the routes (including the new query routes). This contradicts the PR claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and the spec does not justify it.
findings.fix: Restore expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES]). The fakeApp change that records the query string already makes this work with the new routes.

findings.what: The PR body says no tests were loosened and only the fake app was changed to record the query string. The diff also replaces a strict assertion with toBeDefined().
findings.fix: Correct the PR body once the assertion is restored.

findings.what: An empty table on the open or done view costs an extra COUNT query. This is fine functionally. A non-empty-check failure path has no extra handling.

lenses.note: Spec exists with the owner's go; the decisions (open default, query parameter) are followed.
All 8 ACs are implemented and named by tests. Every state row has a test. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-check regex change the new routes require.
The new tests are solid, but traffic.test.js has a loosened assertion that can never fail. I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
README describes the views. The CLAUDE.md conventions (route in routes.json, additive migration) are followed.
The view value is validated against an own-property whitelist, and SQL is built only from constant fragments.
The view parameter is whitelisted, titles are HTML-escaped, and the traffic check still refuses spaces and #.
The page is minimal HTML with no visual design, so I raised nothing here.
The behaviours in the core flow are covered by the Worker-runtime tests. There are no screenshots.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see the tests finding).
